title: Demand-Signal Fair-Share for High-Impact Accounts and Escalation Runway
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and pilot a 'fair-share' demand allocation system that converts account signals into time-boxed roadmap capacity commitments and an escalation runway. Purpose: create predictable, auditable commitments for top accounts while preserving product velocity and avoiding single-customer overcommitment.
background: Repeated ad-hoc escalations from strategic accounts have led to uneven allocation of engineering bandwidth and opaque decisions. Current intake relies on subjective scoring and ad-hoc promises. We need a repeatable mechanism that balances revenue signal, technical dependency, and fairness so sales/CS can set expectations and PM can plan sprints without last-minute rework.
solution_outline: 1) Score incoming requests with a demand-signal vector (deal size, renewal proximity, severity, regulatory requirement, integration complexity). 2) Convert scores into 'runway tokens' that map to roadmap capacity buckets per quarter. 3) Enforce a cap-per-account per quarter and a pooled reserve for emergent escalations. 4) Provide transparent UI and a standard escalation runway process with SLA tiers. 5) Pilot with top 12 accounts for Q1 then iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot scoring rubric published in Confluence and approved by Revenue Ops and Legal
Dashboard showing per-account runway tokens and used capacity for pilot accounts
One completed pilot intake cycle with at least 3 escalations handled through the runway process
No more than 10% unplanned sprint churn attributed to pilot accounts during pilot quarter
Stakeholder signoff (PM, Sales, CS, Eng) on fairness cap rules
milestones: 2025-11-12: finalize scoring rubric and weighting doc (Confluence)
2025-11-20: engineering dependency review and proto API contract (ENG breakout)
2026-03-14: pilot retrospective and decision to expand or iterate
metrics: % of top-account asks that are served from runway tokens vs emergency rework
Sprint churn delta pre/post pilot (goal: <10% increase)
Revenue at-risk reduction for accounts in pilot (qualitative tracking)
roles_and_responsibilities: PM (Aisha): define rubric, run pilot, stakeholder coordination
Revenue Ops: provide deal signals and weighting feedback
Sales/CS: nominate pilot accounts and commit to using intake path
Eng: produce API contract, dashboard telemetry, and capacity enforcement hooks
Legal/Security: review any contractual runway commitments and SLAs
risks: Overfitting rubric to early pilot accounts leading to unfair outcomes at scale
Sales bypassing the system and escalating directly (change management risk)
Engineering capacity enforcement complexity if feature flags/quotas are not implemented before pilot
Customer disappointment if runway tokens are perceived as guarantees without delivery timeline
mitigations: Include a behavioral incentive: billing/renewal advocates get priority only if intake route is followed
Build transparent audit logs and a public pilot FAQ that sets expectations
Start with conservative caps and a small emergent reserve to handle surprises
Run weekly cross-functional sync during pilot to catch complaints early
updates: 2025-11-06: Initial working session with Revenue Ops and Legal; revenue weights proposed (deal size 40%, renewal 25%, severity 20%, strategic fit 15%).
2025-11-10: Engineering outlined two enforcement approaches: soft quotas (dashboard-only) vs hard quotas (enforced in ticketing templates). Decided to start with soft quotas for pilot.
2025-11-14: Design delivered low-fi dashboard; Sales leadership endorsed pilot account list of 12; CS requested a 48hr SLA for escalation acknowledgement.
2025-11-18: PRD v0.2 published. ENG-21488 flagged as dependency for telemetry events; PM-31012 is a downstream playbook update for sales onboarding.
notes_for_future_iterations: Consider integrating runway tokens into the Dedicated contract negotiation flow so customers can buy guaranteed runway units in annual reserved capacity. Long-term, add automated suggestions from console Optimize (e.g., quantization or routing recommendations) to reduce per-request cost and free runway tokens.
